title: Module review
subtitle: Everything from What Wine Is
objectives: Define wine and its alcohol range
Describe how wine is made and where it grows

steps.prompt: What makes a drink wine in the strict, legal sense?
options: The fermentation of fresh grapes or must
steps.explanation: Wine is the fermentation of fresh grapes or grape must. The alcohol level describes most wines but doesn't define them, and distillation makes spirit, not wine.

steps.prompt: Put the winemaking steps in order.
steps.explanation: Fermentation turns juice into wine; maturation is the rest that follows, before bottling.

steps.prompt: Grapes from a warmer place usually make a wine with more alcohol.
steps.explanation: Yes. More heat and sun means more sugar in the berry, and more sugar becomes more alcohol, about 1% for every 17 g/l.

steps.prompt: Which of these are New World wine countries?
steps.explanation: Argentina, South Africa and Australia planted vines with European settlers. Spain and Germany are part of the Old World, where wine culture began.

steps.prompt: The liver clears roughly ____ unit of alcohol per hour.
steps.explanation: About one unit an hour. Coffee, water and fresh air don't change that speed.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Wine is fermented fresh grape juice, usually 11 to 14.5% alcohol
Harvest, pressing, fermentation, maturation and bottling make every wine
Most wine grows between 30 and 50 degrees latitude, in the Old and New Worlds
Know the units in your glass, eat, and spit when tasting
